summary: CPU feature detection (__usercall, ebp-anchored locals): installs a structured exception handler via SEHHandlerInit so the CPUID instruction is guarded against faulting on CPUs without CPUID support, writes the literal "GenuineIntel" into a stack-local vendor buffer, then runs CPUID leaf 0. If the returned max basic leaf is 0 the function returns the feature flags (still 0). Otherwise it runs CPUID leaf 1 and sets flag bit 0x4 when EDX bit 0x2000000 (SSE) is set and flag bit 0x8 when EDX bit 0x4000000 (SSE2) is set, returning the accumulated flags.

operations.description: Call SEHHandlerInit to install a structured exception handler before executing CPUID, guarding against faults on CPUs that lack CPUID support.
Initialize the feature-flags result slot to 0 and set up the SEH registration chain (stack-local frame variables below the ebp anchor).
Copy the literal "GenuineIntel" (aGenuineIntel, 0x005ADE74) into a stack-local vendor buffer.
Execute CPUID leaf 0 with EAX = 0 and store EAX (max basic leaf), EBX, EDX and ECX into stack-local slots.
Code targets loc_50FD9A (0x0050FD9A) and loc_59C724 (0x0059C724) are referenced as SEH filter/continuation targets; the exact fault-handling behavior they implement is not modeled here.
Guard: if CPUID leaf 0 EAX (max basic leaf) is 0, return the current feature flags (0) without probing leaf 1.
Execute CPUID leaf 1 with EAX = 1 and store EAX and EDX into stack-local slots.
If CPUID leaf 1 EDX bit 0x2000000 is set (SSE support), OR flag 0x4 into the feature flags.
If CPUID leaf 1 EDX bit 0x4000000 is set (SSE2 support), OR flag 0x8 into the feature flags.
Called by OSVersionDetection (0x0050FDF3) to query CPU instruction-set features.

unresolved: The strcpy of "GenuineIntel" fills a stack-local vendor buffer, but no comparison against the CPUID leaf 0 vendor registers (EBX/EDX/ECX) is visible in this fragment, so the buffer's consumer is unknown.
loc_50FD9A and loc_59C724 are SEH filter/continuation code targets whose exception-handling semantics are not modeled.
The ebp-anchored stack slots (a1 offsets) are __usercall frame locals, not object fields; their exact types are unknown.
Meaning of the returned flags beyond the SSE/SSE2 bits is not established.
